clue.text: Want starter of risotto in the end

indicators.note: in says the opening letter goes inside the word for the end

parts.note: death is the end of life

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so this takes the opening letter of risotto

explanation.surface: Someone complains of a lack of food, with only a taste of risotto right at the end of the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity, and want in the noun sense means lack or shortage.

clue.text: Sadly, minor is overwhelmed by homework?

indicators.note: something overwhelmed is engulfed, so the word for minor goes inside

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is work done on one's home
minor means small

explanation.surface: A child is sadly swamped by schoolwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'homework' is not school work but DIY, work on the home.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismally means in a gloomy, miserable way, so sadly.

clue.text: Plenty of cake following a social occasion

indicators.note: following puts the cake after the a, before the occasion

parts.note: a bun is a small cake
a dance is a social event

explanation.surface: Lots of cake after a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance is a large quantity, more than enough, which is plenty.

clue.text: Ditch fish in river? The opposite

indicators.note: in would put the fish inside the river letter
The opposite reverses that, so the river letter goes inside the fish

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Is a fish in a river or a ditch?
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow ditch dug in the ground.

clue.text: A dog tucked into bread and fruit

indicators.note: tucked into means the first pieces are slipped inside the word for bread

parts.note: bread is slang for money, cash
a Lab is a Labrador, a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A dog wolfs down some bread and a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' looks like food beside 'fruit' but is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A calabash is a gourd, the hard-shelled fruit of a tropical tree or vine.

clue.text: Fools one community of people to make a killing

parts.note: fools in the plural gives two asses, ass and ass
I is the Roman numeral for one
a nation is a large community of people

explanation.surface: Idiots join a whole population to make a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a killing' suggests profit, but here the killing is a murder.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassination is the murder of a prominent person, a killing.

clue.text: After a month, one needs bed for fruit tree

indicators.note: After puts the one letter after the month

parts.note: Apr is the abbreviation for April
I is the Roman numeral for one
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: After a month, someone needs a bed under a fruit tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The apricot is a tree of the rose family bearing orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Song and dance about love

parts.note: a song and dance is a fuss, ado
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A musical number about love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song and dance' is a fuss, not a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore is to love deeply, so the verb fits love.

clue.text: Runs into house to catch insect

indicators.note: into says the runs letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: to net is to catch
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone dashes into a house to trap an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A hornet is a large stinging wasp, an insect.

clue.text: Lip dressing

explanation.surface: Seems to name a cosmetic product for the lips.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce means both cheek or backchat and a liquid condiment poured over food.

clue.text: Energy is harnessed by flowing rivers or lake

indicators.note: something harnessed is held within, so E sits inside the shuffled letters
flowing suggests the letters of rivers or move about freely

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Hydroelectric power from rivers running into a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowing' looks like a description of rivers but is the anagram signal, and 'lake' is the definition, not more water in the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is an artificial lake built to store water.

clue.text: When wound up, bite as other wants it?

definitions.text: When wound up, bite as other wants it?

indicators.note: wants means needs, so it is added to the anagram
wound up means twisted round, so the letters of bite as other are rearranged

explanation.surface: An angler's fish snaps at the lure just as the angler hoped.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a teased person bites, as the teaser wants.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise to the bait is to react to provocation, as a fish rises to a lure.

clue.text: To sum up, it's about the ultimate for Mac users

parts.note: to sum up figures is to add them

indicators.note: about means the letters of it's go around the final letter

parts.note: it's taken as its letters without the apostrophe

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so this takes the final letter of Mac

explanation.surface: A summary claiming something is the best thing ever for owners of Apple computers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ITS around C, the last letter of Mac.
explanation.definitionFit: Addicts are habitual drug users, so the plural noun fits users.

clue.text: Swimmer to give someone a mouse?

parts.note: to sock someone is to punch them, to give them one
a mouse is slang for a black eye, so the punch lands on the eye

explanation.surface: Seems to ask whether a pet mouse makes a good present for a swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give someone a mouse' means give them a black eye: SOCK them in the EYE.
explanation.definitionFit: The sockeye is a Pacific salmon, a fish and so a swimmer.

clue.text: Secure network connected with Germany

parts.note: a LAN is a local area network of computers
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A secure computer network has been linked up with Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: To land a deal or a fish is to secure or obtain it.

clue.text: Tipsy on vacation, shed attire and streaked

indicators.note: tipsy means wobbly with drink, so the letters stagger into a new order
vacated means emptied, so shed loses its middle and keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A drunk holidaymaker strips off and goes streaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties SHED to SD; 'Tipsy' shuffles SD with ATTIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Striated means marked with parallel lines or bands, that is streaked.

clue.text: Cruel one with no heart? That's reflected by article

indicators.note: by means next to, so the article comes beside the turned pieces
reflected means mirrored, so the letters of the first pieces read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a heart is a playing card
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Asks whether a heartless person is mirrored in an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no heart' looks like heartless, but a heart is a CARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Draconian means excessively harsh, from Draco's severe laws, so cruel.

clue.text: Famous person saving British expedition

indicators.note: saving means except, so the British letter is left out

parts.note: a celebrity is a famous person

explanation.surface: A celebrity rescues a British expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' means except, not rescuing; 'expedition' means speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition in its old sense is promptness, haste, which celerity means.

clue.text: English mercenary securing trade union's future

indicators.note: securing means holding on to, so the union letters are held inside the word for mercenary

parts.note: venal means willing to be bought, mercenary
TU is the abbreviation for trade union

explanation.surface: A hired English soldier guarantees the future of a labour union.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventual as an adjective means happening later on, ultimately, so future in the sense of yet to come.

clue.text: Cast lie about being flexible

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters of cast lie are rearranged

explanation.surface: Telling a lie about being bendy.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic means stretchy and able to spring back, so flexible.

clue.text: Exposed stomach to the audience

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to stomach something is to tolerate or bear it

explanation.surface: A performer shows off their belly to the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stomach' is a verb, tolerate, not a belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare means uncovered, exposed to view.

clue.text: To call forth speaker's not allowed

indicators.note: a speaker's word is spoken, so it is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: illicit means forbidden, not allowed

explanation.surface: A speaker may not shout out.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out or evoke a response, which is to call forth.

clue.text: I therefore exclude what's seen on some maps

parts.note: so means therefore
to bar is to exclude

explanation.surface: A logician decides to rule out what's shown on certain maps.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line of equal pressure drawn on weather charts.

clue.text: Cattle roaming around area produce milk

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters go round the abbreviation for area
roaming means wandering about, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Cows wandering about the field make milk.
explanation.definitionFit: To lactate is to secrete milk from the mammary glands.

clue.text: Cleric's ecclesiastical law

definitions.meaning: a clergyman attached to a cathedral
a rule or law of the Church

explanation.definitionFit: Canon names both a cathedral clergyman and a decree of Church law.

clue.text: Around November, is rent imminent?

indicators.note: Around means the following letters go round the November letter

parts.note: N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet
rent here is the past tense of rend, so torn: tore

explanation.surface: A tenant asks whether rent is due around November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' is not payment but the past of rend, so TORE.
explanation.definitionFit: In store means coming soon, about to happen, as in trouble in store.

clue.text: Limit what happens in prison gym?

parts.note: in a prison gym the inmates, cons, exercise or train: read the result as two words

explanation.surface: Asks how far a prison exercise session may go.
explanation.walkthrough: What happens in a prison gym? CONS TRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain is to restrict or hold back, so limit as a verb.

clue.text: Intrinsic to Dublin, Irish pancake

indicators.note: Intrinsic to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pancake said to be typical of the Irish capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Blini are small Russian buckwheat pancakes, often served with caviar.

clue.text: Manchester and Bristol teams both one man short? Persistence needed

parts.note: a football team has eleven players, so one man short leaves ten
Manchester City and Bristol City are both a City

explanation.surface: Two football sides each down to ten men will need to dig in.
explanation.walkthrough: Each team is A CITY with TEN men. Manchester City and Bristol City are English football clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacity is the quality of holding on firmly, determination, so persistence.

clue.text: Bishop wants hot drink

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
hot can mean sexually aroused, randy

explanation.surface: A cleric asks for a hot beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine, an alcoholic drink.
